text.p: Grain and oilseed exports reported by USDA and private export sources.

WHEAT/BARLEY SALE - Japan's Food Agency said on Thursday it bought 80,000 tonnes of U.S. wheat, 20,000 tonnes of Canadian wheat, 20,000 tonnes of Australian wheat, 20,000 tonnes of U.S. barley and 40,000 tonnes of Australian barley at its weekly tender. They are all for September shipment.
SOYBEAN SALE - USDA in its weekly export sales report said net soybean sales to China for delivery during the 1997/98 marketing year totalled 52,500 tonnes in the week to July 10.
SOYMEAL TENDER - CCC was seeking up to 7,000 tonnes of U.S. soybean meal in bulk for donation to Nicaragua. The shipment was slated for August 10-30. Offers were due July 23.

WHEAT/BARLEY TENDER - The Food Agency of Japan said it will not carry out its weekly import tender for wheat and barley set for July 24, as it has finished buying all of its requirements for September shipment. The agency will resume its grain import tender from July 31 for October shipment.
WHEAT TENDERS - Pakistan on July 28 would be seeking a total of 500,000 tonnes optional origin wheat for August 11 to September 10 shipment, a Pakistan embassy official said.

WHEAT TENDERS cont'd - South Africa's Wheat Board was offering 49,756 tonnes of wheat for sale and delivery before August 31. The wheat is being offered for sale domestically or for export from various depots around the country. The tender closes on July 18.

- The CCC said it was seeking up to 6,360 tonnes of U.S. no. 2 or better hard red winter wheat for donation to Tunisia. The shipment period was slated for August 10-August 31. Offers were due on July 22, it said.

WHEAT TENDERS - Jordan is scheduled to tender July 23 for 100,000 tonnes of U.S. hard red winter or hard red spring wheat or equivalent wheat from other countries, U.S. exporters said. Half of the tonnage was slated for last-half August shipment and the balance for last-half September shipment.

- Algeria has launched a tender for the import of 75,000 tonnes of optional soft wheat for September shipment, European grain traders said. Exporters also said Algeria was seeking 150,000 tonnes of durum wheat for shipment in August and September. Results of both tenders were due later this week.

CORN/SOYBEAN TENDER - The Egyptian state's Food Industries Company was seeking 30,000 tonnes of U.S. or Argentine No. 2 yellow corn for arrival in the second half of September and/or the second half of October and 30,000 tonnes of soybean, any origin, for arrival first half of October and/or first half November. The deadline for bids is July 22.

RICE TENDERS - Syria's General Foreign Trade Organisation for Chemicals and Foodstuffs will receive offers until July 23 to buy 24,000 tonnes of white rice for August delivery, a GEZA spokesman said. Results would be available on July 24.
The CCC said it was seeking on July 22 a total of 1,780 tonnes U.S. long grain rice for donation to Burkina Faso. The shipment period was for August 21 to September 5.

MARKET TALK - The Egyptian state has decreed that it will require imports of commodities meant for human consumption to be accompanied by proof that genetic engineering was not used in their production. Existing Egyptian export business with the United States has not yet been affected by an Egyptian state decree barring imports of genetically altered grains and soybeans, several U.S. exporters said. USDA said it was pressing for a meeting with Egypt for clarification.

... Pakistan wheat demand should remain firm in the 1997/98 season and lower wheat prices may tempt Islamabad to rebuild stocks, an economist with the USDA said in an interview in a Singapore wheat conference. He added prospects for U.S. wheat sales in 1998 look rosy because of an expected fall in output in Argentina and Australia.
... India, boosted by a good wheat crop, timely imports and good rainfall, has comfortable foodgrain stocks and is unlikely to seek more imports this fiscal year, traders and analysts said.
